literal.prompt: Какое правило помогает посетителям защищать диких животных в национальном парке?
answers: Не кормить животных и убирать еду и мусор туда, где они не смогут их достать.
Оставлять пищевые отходы у кромки стоянки, подальше от палаток.
Подкармливать птиц и мелких животных только крошками.
Кормить животных лишь пищей, подходящей их естественному рациону.

literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS L23-L25 establishes park-visitor responsibility and wildlife protection; NPS L42-L45 and NPWS L121-L127,L172-L175 support the no-feeding/secure-food rule and reject feeding/leftover alternatives.

literalGroups.literal: Правильный ответ: не кормить животных и убирать еду и мусор туда, где они не смогут до них добраться. NPS указывает, что здоровый рацион животные получают, охотясь, собирая или подбирая пищу самостоятельно. Привычка искать человеческую еду может сделать животных опасными.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS L43 states natural hunting/foraging/scavenging; L45 describes danger from food conditioning. Both directly support the two explanatory reasons.

literalGroups.literal: Животные, привыкшие искать человеческую пищу, могут стать опасными; в крайних случаях администрация парка вынуждена их удалять.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS L45-L46 supports danger and removal of food-conditioned animals; NPWS L158-L159 independently reports aggression in hand-fed animals.

literalGroups.literal: Оставленный мусор тоже становится доступной животным человеческой пищей и связан с плохим питанием и болезнями.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS L43-L44 directly includes unsecured trash as human food and poor nourishment. New NPWS L132-L133 says human processed food disrupts natural diet and can make wildlife very sick; L163 says a campsite/walk becoming a reliable food source can increase animal density and disease spread; L172 expressly warns against uneaten food and rotting leftovers. This supports a contextual association, not a claim that every scrap directly infects an animal.

literalGroups.literal: Даже крошки и объедки — человеческая пища; NPS связывает её с плохим питанием и более короткой жизнью животных.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS L43 names scraps and crumbs offered to birds/other wildlife and states poor nourishment/shorter lives. NPWS L132-L133 gives concrete illness/death effects from processed human food.

literalGroups.literal: Здоровый рацион дикие животные получают, охотясь, собирая или подбирая пищу естественным образом, а не привыкая к человеку.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NPS L43 says healthy diets come from natural hunting, foraging or scavenging; L45 explains food-conditioning. NPWS L143-L144 describes reduced foraging, dependence on handouts and starvation despite natural food.

absoluteDifficulty.audienceGround: Broad adult visitor knowledge: do not feed wildlife and keep food/waste inaccessible in a national park. No specialist ecology terminology or multi-step reasoning.
absoluteDifficulty.reasoning: Select one straightforward visitor-protection action among four plausible parallel rules; official park guidance states the action plainly.

evidenceOnlyDecision.personalFinding: New NPWS primary fills the specific note1 evidence gap through two distinct links: human processed food can disrupt natural diet and make wildlife sick (L132-L133), while feeding that makes a campsite/walk a reliable food source can increase animal density and spread disease (L163). NPS separately says unsecured trash is human food and can cause poor nourishment (L43-L44); NPWS explicitly warns against uneaten food and rotting leftovers (L172). The current wording says “связан” (associated); it does not say that each piece of trash directly infects wildlife. The precise disease mechanism remains the site-level food-source/density association described by NPWS, not ingestion of trash. Thus the unchanged note is supported as a qualified association.
evidenceOnlyDecision.priorGapDistinction: NPS L32 links disease exposure to proximity to people/pets, not eating trash; the new evidence comes from NSW NPWS L132-L133 and L163 plus leftover-food context L172. This author independently read both complete pages; no prior verdict was adopted.
